name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text: I’ll audit the current link coverage baseline by running `make coverage` on the repo root, then parse the HTML report to extract the exact % of links covered. If it’s below 95%, I’ll open `docs/coverage_report.md` and append a TODO list with filenames and line numbers needing link checks—starting with `src/cli/parser.py` (lines 42-67) where 12 of 18 links are untested.

name: Scriv
text: Scriv: Hold—your plan hinges on `make coverage` producing a *reliable* HTML report, but what if the build system’s coverage tool is misconfigured or the report’s parsing logic fails on edge cases (e.g., dynamically generated links, redirects, or non-HTTP schemes)? Demand evidence: run `make coverage` *twice* on a clean checkout and diff the reports to prove idempotency before trusting the baseline. If the variance exceeds 1%, the tool itself is the risk—not the coverage gap.
